alex: Heads up — after yesterday's routing policy swap (priority -> latency-first) we're seeing a recurring tail in invoice-preview for some tenants (~25-40s). Not a full outage but invoices missing last-minute tokens.

maya: Hmm. Is this the change that moved 2% of traffic to the edge-shard fallback?

alex: yes, the fallback route that uses relaxed fingerprinting (v2) for throughput. The issue shows up only for tenants with high session churn.

jp: Can you paste a trace id? I want to check the routing hops and whether the enrichment fanout is delaying finalization.

alex: trace=trace_2024942. See tail of query plan in logs:```
[ingest] route=priority-fallback v=2 shard=eu-west-1
[fanout] enrichers=3 pending=1 wait_ms=22000
[finalize] window_wait_ms=12000 commit=delayed
```

tessa: 22s wait on enrichers + 12s window wait explains 34s tail. Why are enrichers pending? we batch them to 50ms normally.

maya: Likely because the fallback path uses a sync enrichment that can't use the async cache. Routing policy change increased the path length.

jp: Two quick follow-ups: 1) What's sampling behavior for preview mode? If preview is higher fidelity we might be forcing sync enrich for those previews. 2) Are we buffering tokens in memqueue until enrichment ack?

alex: Preview mode sets sampling_rate=1 (no sampling) and preview_finalizer forces sync enrich to get exact token attribution. Yes we buffer until enrichment ack — to avoid double-counting.

maya: That buffering plus a slow enrich path would explain missing tokens in the invoice snapshot when the committer times out and finalizer rolls back.

billing-bot: alert: invoice-preview latency p95 crossed 30s for tenant t-402 at 2024-11-07T15:22:10Z :warning:

jp: Proposed mitigations: A) revert the routing change for fallback path to keep old fingerprinting for canary tenants, B) make preview_finalizer permissive (accept async enrichment results with later reconciliation), or C) introduce a small, guaranteed fallback cache for v2 path so enrichers return quickly.

tessa: (B) seems the least disruptive and keeps the routing test in place. We do need reconciler work to avoid eventual double-counting — would require an idempotent enrichment token id.

maya: For (C) could we do a tiny KV cache co-located on edge-shard? 1k entries LRU per shard -> hits for 60% of churny sessions. Might shave 10-15s.

jp: Cache sounds reasonable but is more infra work. For short term, can we change preview_finalizer to not block on enrichment longer than 3s and instead emit an "incomplete_preview" flag in invoice-preview? Console teams can show a yellow badge and explain delayed attribution.

alex: I like that — gives UX visibility and avoids blocking commits. Also lets us track reconciliation rate.

maya: I'll open a tiny UX ticket for console: show "attribution pending" with link to preview-telemetry. Can we include the trace id so support can drill?

tessa: I'll implement the code change — add timeout=3000ms and emit metadata {preview_status: "pending_enrich", trace_id}. Also add a metric meter.preview_incomplete{route,fallback_reason}.

jp: I'll add a temporary alert on the reconciler that fires if reconciled_token_delta > 0.5% for 5m. We need to catch regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy starting for service=ingest-finalizer version=2024.11.08-canary-build at 2024-11-08T01:05:00Z :rocket:

alex: Great. Plan: tessa pushes canary with 3s timeout to canary group (same tenants that saw the initial routing), we'll monitor p95 and invoice diffs, and jp's reconciliation alert will catch any surge.

maya: Also document this in the rollout notes: note that preview mode will surface "pending" state for up to 24h while background recon runs. Ops will have a tool to force reconcile for critical invoices.

alex: Thanks team — ping me in this thread if you see any anomalies. :eyes:
